(1) the localization accuracy of an automatic localizer has a significant influence on the accuracy of a far field speech recognition system; and (2) combining video with audio features significantly improves the accuracy of the localizer.

(i) the accuracy of a speaker localization system is crucial for minimizing error rate in far field ASR, and (ii) a combination of audio features and visual features provides the best accuracy in speaker localization.
the combination of audio and visual features is most suitable for localization and that localization is crucial to minimize the word error rate of a microphone array driven speech recognition system.

the influence of speaker localization on the word error rates of far field speech recognition systems.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WER is reduced by about 50% by using a localization system that is based on audio and video information compared to a system that only uses audio information.

the combination of audio and visual features is the most accurate localization technique for the considered data set, but the WER of a far field speech recognition system does not significantly benefit from the use of a visual localizer.
the best performance is obtained with a system based on both audio and video features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of audio and visual features is a promising approach for accurate speaker localization, which in turn leads to a reduction of the word error rate for far field ASR systems.
the WER of a far field speech recognition system can be reduced by combining the information from audio and video features.
the WER of the far field ASR is highly dependent on the accuracy of the speaker localization system.

the WER is not only influenced by the accuracy of the source localization, but also by the localization method.
